sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Out-of-Gauge (OOG) Heavy Industrial Project Cargo Logistics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong influence of European Union Regulations and Grand-Ducal implementing decrees)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) bilateral investment treaties with third countries
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) for covered tax agreements
EU-Luxembourg and third-country double tax treaties (notably US, Germany, France, Netherlands)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the organization and operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation (EU) 2015/849 and successive Luxembourg AML/CFT implementing circulars

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign certified copy of a legal entity partner's certificate of incorporation and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign trade registrar or competent companies registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the SCSp representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address and bank reference for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certified translation of notarized document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, and SCSp representatives against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, and Luxembourg domestic sanctions under CSSF guidance. Enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons as defined under FATF Recommendation 12 and AML Law of 2004, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, low-risk project cargo logistics designation notwithstanding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed SCSp name must be written in Latin alphabetic characters, must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not contain misleading elements, and must end with the mandatory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' to comply with the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commercial banks sensitive terms requiring prior ministerial or CSSF approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant receives a formal written refusal with grounds. The applicant may lodge an administrative appeal with the Tribunal de l'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) within fifteen days of notification. In the alternative, the applicant may submit a fresh application with revised amendments, subject to payment of a new statutory fee. Further appellate review is available before the Luxembourg Court of Appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is permissible solely in the form of a professional domiciliation service provided by a licensed statutory agent. A pure virtual mail-forwarding address is insufficient for commercial substance. For SCSp used in project cargo logistics, the registered office in Luxembourg must be a physical address where corporate records may be inspected by the Luxembourg Commercial Court and administrative authorities; however, a shared office or business-center arrangement is acceptable without dedicated operational staff. Tax treaty eligibility requires economic substance, including actual decision-making or management in Luxembourg, although for low-risk logistics holding vehicles the initial phase may rely on a domiciliation service until operations commence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and name reservation application at RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under Grand-Ducal Regulation on commercial and company register tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Incidental cost per supporting document, approximate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Luxembourg Companies Act), including the SCSp provisions introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies and on accounting records; Law of 22 March 2017 on the business establishment authorisation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 9 rue du Commerce, L-1359 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés supported by the executed formation deed and Limited Partnership Agreement; publication extract in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. An SCSp is not a capital company and has no statutory minimum paid-up capital, no subscribed capital threshold, and no mandatory escrow account rule. Capital contributions are defined in the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be called in cash or in kind. The use of a bank or escrow account is a contractual matter between the partners and the bank, not a statutory formation condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial partners and managers of LU SCSp Heavy Haul, acting by unanimous written consent, adopt this First Board Resolution effective upon RCS registration. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership is fixed at [registered address] in Luxembourg; the partners approve the subscription of partnership interests and capital contributions in accordance with the Limited Partnership Agreement, and any excess funds shall be held in escrow until called. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed General Manager, with authority to open bank accounts, accept milestone wire payments and letters of credit, engage advisors, and execute filings before the RCS, tax authorities, and administrative authorities. RESOLVED, that all acts of the General Manager done before this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the SCSp name and validate availability with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - eJustice online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the eJustice RCS filing portal and submit up to three proposed names in priority order, each including 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the suffix 'SCSp'. The RCS verifies that the proposed name is available, not misleading, and not identical to an existing registered name. Once the name is accepted, obtain the name reservation certificate which is valid for a limited statutory reservation period.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in priority order
Identification details of the applicants or authorised representative
Power of attorney of the local RCS agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, promptly submit alternative names through the same portal or provide counsel's written opinion on distinctiveness. If the reservation lapses, submit a new name reservation request; no court remedy is required for a name refusal unless a distinctiveness dispute is raised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the formation deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary selected by the partners; private deed may be used to the extent permitted for an SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the formation deed (acte constitutif) and the Limited Partnership Agreement (contrat de société). Execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary or by private written deed where notarisation is not mandatory for the assets concerned. The formation documents must state the registered office in Luxembourg, the object clause covering out-of-gauge project cargo logistics support (ISIC 5229), the duration, the contribution schedule, the identity of the general partner and limited partners, and the persons authorised to manage the SCSp. All partners must sign, or, if a corporate partner is involved, its legally authorised representatives must produce the relevant corporate authorisations.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each partner and each beneficial owner
Proof of address of each partner
Tax identification number or equivalent of each partner
Articles of association and current extract from the foreign business register for any corporate general partner
Good standing and criminal record statement for each individual manager
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Evidence of contribution arrangements or escrow instruction letter, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the parties identify inconsistencies, execute a rectification deed or a restated Limited Partnership Agreement before submitting to the RCS. Missing partner consents may be cured by supplemental written partner resolutions signed on the same date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the initial RCS registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - eJustice online portal or RCS front desk counters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed formation deed and Limited Partnership Agreement on the eJustice portal and complete the standard RCS registration form. State the registered office address, the business object, the general partner and branches, the officers, and the date of the formation deed. Where the formation deed is notarised, attach the notarial copy; where private, attach the scanned deed signed by all partners. The RCS examiner verifies legal formalities and publishes the registration notice in the RESA electronic official gazette. The SCSp obtains its RCS registration number and registration certificate upon completion.
required_dossiers: Executed formation deed or certified notarial copy
Limited Partnership Agreement
Completed RCS initial registration form
Registered office consent from the lessor or owner
Identity documents of the partners and managers
Certified copy of the name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (régularisation), respond through eJustice within eight days with the requested corrections or additional evidence. If the RCS refuses registration, the applicant may appeal to the President of the Luxembourg District Court or re-file a corrected deed; legal counsel should coordinate the remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the certified RCS excerpt and RESA publication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - RESA publication desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registration is completed, the RCS automatically publishes the legal notice in the RESA electronic gazette. Order a certified copy of the RCS excerpt (extrait du RCS) evidencing the formation of the SCSp, its number, and the authorised officers. This certified excerpt is the primary evidence of existence used for banking, tax, licensing, and client onboarding purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RESA publication extract
Filing number or order reference from eJustice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or the excerpt contains errors, contact LBR-RCS support to obtain a state-of-file confirmation and request a rectification of the entry. Any material mistake in the registered information must be corrected by filing a rectification form or supplemental deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the RCS registration, file the initial taxpayer registration with the ACD to obtain the Luxembourg fiscal number and, if necessary, the corporate income tax file. Submit the VAT registration application with the AEDT using the eCDF platform to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number. If the SCSp will employ staff, register as an employer with the CCSS and set up the payroll declaration account. The SCSp is treated as fiscally transparent for income tax purposes in Luxembourg, but must still maintain its own tax file and, as applicable, VAT identification for the activities carried on.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS excerpt
Formation deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
Identity and residency information of the partners
Description of the business activities in Luxembourg
Tax identification numbers of the partners
Employer registration form and payroll information, if employees will be engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities query the registration, provide the requested information within 15 days through the AEDT or ACD portal. Late registrations may be corrected voluntarily where no tax liability is outstanding; legal counsel may assist in negotiating penalties if the delay is reasonable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the initial beneficial owner declaration with the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the eJustice RBE portal and file the initial declaration of beneficial owners within the statutory deadline following registration. Identify every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls more than 25 percent of the partnership interests, voting rights, or capital. Provide name, date and place of birth, nationality, residential address, the nature and extent of the interest, and supporting documentary evidence. The RBE information must be kept current and updated within one month of any change.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS excerpt
Partnership ownership and control structure chart
Passport or identity card of each beneficial owner
Supporting evidence of the beneficial ownership percentage
Completed RBE online form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE service raises a query, submit a corrective declaration with the additional evidence requested. Rectification after filing is accepted for good-faith errors; repeated or intentional failure to file may result in criminal fines, so counsel should ensure prompt compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the establishment authorisation and any incidental transport licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des Classes moyennes et de l'Entrepreneuriat (DGCME); for road transport operations, Ministry of Mobility and Public Works
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the establishment authorisation under the Luxembourg Law of 22 March 2017 on the business establishment authorisation. Demonstrate that the general partner and the person responsible for daily management meet the requirements of good character, professional competence, and absence of criminal conviction. For the ISIC 5229 project-cargo logistics scope, no sectoral banking or financial licence is required; however, if the SCSp will operate heavy goods vehicles for own-account road haulage, apply separately to the transport authority for the appropriate EU Community licence and financial standing evidence.
required_dossiers: Completed DGCME establishment authorisation application form
Certified RCS excerpt
Criminal record extracts for the managers or general partner representatives
Evidence of professional competence and relevant logistics experience
Certificate of tax and social security compliance
Proof of the business premises and site layout
EU Community licence application and financial statements, if road haulage is to be performed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGCME requests further information, respond through the online portal within the stated deadline. If the authorisation is refused, appeal to the Luxembourg administrative court within three months; before appeal, counsel may submit additional evidence of professional capacity or restructuring of the management function.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete corporate bank account opening and AML/KYC onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A CSSF-regulated Luxembourg credit institution or select payment institution/e-money institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the SCSp's bank or payment account presenting the certified RCS excerpt, formation deed, Limited Partnership Agreement, RBE declaration, and identification documents of the general partner, managers, and beneficial owners. Execute the bank mandate and set the authorised signatories. Configure payment rails for milestone wire transfers and documentary letters of credit. The bank will perform customer due diligence and source-of-funds checks in accordance with Luxembourg anti-money laundering rules and may request a brief business plan.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS excerpt
Formation deed and Limited Partnership Agreement
RBE declaration confirmation
Passports or identity cards of partners, managers, and beneficial owners
Proof of the registered office address
Business plan and source of funds statement
Bank reference letter or prior board resolution authorising the account mandate, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide additional source-of-funds evidence and explanations of the corporate structure. If the bank declines the relationship, engage another Luxembourg credit institution or a CSSF-regulated payment institution and update the account mandate accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des Classes moyennes et de l'Entrepreneuriat (DGCME); sectoral coordination with the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works for road transport operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 22 March 2017; where applicable, EU Community licence for road haulage of heavy and out-of-gauge project cargo

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or exemption expected for the project-cargo logistics support operation unless the project exceeds the thresholds of the Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. A full EIA report will be required only if the activity includes a classified installation such as large-scale storage or hazardous goods handling reaching the applicable Annex thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal wastewater discharge limits applicable to the registered site, with typical limits of pH 6.0-9.5, COD not exceeding 1,000 mg/l, and suspended solids not exceeding 600 mg/l unless stricter local by-laws apply. Volatile organic compound emissions, if any, must remain below the VOC solvent threshold under the Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing EU Directive 2010/75/EU. All waste, including non-hazardous cargo residues and used oil, must be handled through registered waste operators in accordance with the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The operating site must obtain a municipal fire safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie), pass a structural load review for crane pads, heavy-lift yards, and racking installations, and complete an occupational safety inspection by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (Inspection du travail et des mines - ITM) before commencement of physical cargo handling activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg tax registration is split across three administrations. (1) Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes, address: 33 rue de Gasperich, L-5826 Hesperange, portal: impotsdirects.public.lu. (2) Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties, VAT desk: Bureau d'imposition TVA, 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg, portal: aed.public.lu. (3) Administration des Douanes et Accises (ADA) for customs duties and EORI issuance, portal: douanes.public.lu. All statutory filings are electronically routed through the official single State gateway MyGuichet.lu (myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - RCS Trade Register: file the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de societe; private deed suffices, no notarial act required unless real estate contributes) with the Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu; RCS registration automatically generates the Luxembourg national tax identification number (matricule / numéro d'identification national) from the Registre National des Personnes Morales (RNM). Step 2 - VAT registration: submit Form 642 (Demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA) to AEDT with the RCS excerpt, partnership agreement, identity of partners and gérant, and bank confirmation; a foreign non-established taxable person may register directly, but must appoint an approved Luxembourg fiscal representative if established outside the EU/EEA; VAT number format: LU + 8 digits. Step 3 - EORI: apply to the Customs Administration (ADA) for a Luxembourg EORI number (format LU + 10 digits), required for every export declaration, obtainable through MyGuichet or the EU customs portal. Step 4 - Employer/social security: if the SCSp hires personnel, register as employer with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) and with ACD for withholding tax. Processing times: RCS 5-10 business days; VAT number 5-15 business days after complete submission; EORI 2-5 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible | Territorial_Scope: an SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct tax because it has no legal personality; income, gains and net wealth are allocated pro-rata to partners and taxed in their hands, and the SCSp itself is not subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IBC) or net wealth tax (IFI). The general partner (commandité) is taxed on its allocated share as commercial profits (residence-based); non-resident limited partners (commanditaires) are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income, which for an SCSp is limited to Luxembourg real estate, Luxembourg permanent establishment income and certain Luxembourg-source royalties. Tax_Exempt_Zone: no Luxembourg free-zone or special economic zone exemption is available to the SCSp; however, if the SCSp is structured as a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF/SIF) the transparency mechanism ensures tax neutrality at fund level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; transparency of the SCSp is mandatory for direct-tax purposes. Available elections: (i) VAT option - under Article 12 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, a transparent partnership conducting an economic activity may register for VAT and exercise input-deduction rights (option pour la TVA), which is binding for at least five years; (ii) VAT grouping - Article 59 of the VAT Law permits financially, economically and organisationally linked entities to elect a single taxable person (assujetti unique); (iii) OSS/IOSS - optional registration for intra-EU distance sales of goods (annual threshold EUR 10,000) and for imports of low-value consignments, so avoiding multiple EU VAT registrations; (iv) hybrid mismatch alignment - Luxembourg's ATAD 2 provisions (LIR Articles 168a and 168b, Section Vbis) automatically deny deductions to the extent a hybrid entity or instrument causes double non-taxation; no elective reverse-hybrid treatment is available at SCSp level, but the SCSp may obtain a Luxembourg certificate of fiscal residence/allocation of income under double tax treaties to evidence transparency to foreign tax authorities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, fully harmonised with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the AEDT; cross-border services follow EU place-of-supply rules and the Union Customs Code for goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established taxable persons: small business franchise exemption (Article 57 VAT Law) applies up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover (effective 1 January 2023; formerly EUR 30,000). Non-established foreign taxable persons: NO threshold - mandatory VAT registration from the first euro of taxable supplies in Luxembourg. Intra-EU distance sales of goods by Luxembourg sellers: EUR 10,000 annual threshold, above which OSS registration is required. Exports and qualifying international transport services are zero-rated without registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is legally equivalent to paper, but mandatory only for B2G supplies to Luxembourg public authorities (PEPPOL / EN 16931 e-inv format). For B2B taxpayers, e-invoicing is voluntary and can be issued through private billing systems; Luxembourg currently imposes no SAF-T obligation. Customs clearance uses EU UCC electronic systems: DUO/PLDA for export declarations and NCTS for transit. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, mandatory B2B e-invoicing and transaction-based digital reporting through an EU standard system is projected to enter into force on 1 July 2030 (goods) and phases thereafter; taxpayers should prepare their ERP/invoicing interfaces for this future API-based reporting mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to outside the EU are exempt with deduction (zero-rated) under Article 44(1)(a) of the Luxembourg VAT Law (implementing Article 146 of the VAT Directive). Zero-rating also covers international transport of goods and ancillary services (loading, handling, freight forwarding) under Articles 44(1)(b), 44(1)(c) and 45(1)(e) of the VAT Law. For OOG/project cargo heavy-haul logistics, the 0% rate applies when the transport and handling form part of a single export contract and are evidenced by a customs export declaration and transport documents; B2B logistics services to a non-EU principal are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under Article 58 of the VAT Law (place of supply - recipient location), while services physically performed in Luxembourg and not directly linked to an export remain taxable at 17%. Conditions to claim zero-rating: (i) goods must physically leave the EU; (ii) dispatch must occur by or on behalf of the supplier/exporter; (iii) the supplier must hold complete documentary proof (validated MRN, transport contract, commercial invoice, arrival evidence); (iv) the documentary proof must be obtained within 90 days of the time of supply (Article 335 of EU Implementing Regulation 282/2011; Luxembourg administrative practice, extension possible only with justified cause).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document filed via DUO/PLDA with validated Movement Reference Number - MRN)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or CMR / Air Waybill (alternative transport evidence per Incoterms; multimodal bills of lading for OOG project cargo accepted)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT / MT103 payment confirmation evidencing inward settlement of the export proceeds
Commercial invoice and detailed OOG packing list (dimensions, weight, cargo marks and numbers)
Proof of arrival at the third-country destination (port warehouse receipt, customs entry stamp at destination, or third-party delivery confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax audits (AEDT for VAT/customs, ACD for direct taxes) apply strict documentary scrutiny to zero-rated export transactions under Articles 44 et seq. of the VAT Law and EU Implementing Regulation 282/2011. If the exporter cannot produce the full evidence trail (MRN, transport documents, arrival proof, payment evidence), the supply is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply at 17%, with VAT assessed together with late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (Article 53 VAT Law). Retrospective assessment windows: standard five-year period (Article 82 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law - AO), extended to ten years in cases of fraudulent concealment. Administrative fines under Articles 67-69 of the VAT Law may reach 100% of the tax evaded in bad-faith cases, and criminal tax fraud (fraude fiscale) under Article 396 AO / Article 489 of the Criminal Code carries fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Individual liability may extend to the gérant and general partner, and the EORI number or export licence may be suspended. Mitigation: maintain a complete and timely export file (MRN, B/L or CMR, SWIFT proofs of inward freight settlement), honour the 180-day FX settlement convention used in the project-cargo milestone credit terms (this 180-day deadline is a trade-settlement contract norm, not a hard Luxembourg VAT deadline; the hard VAT proof deadline is 90 days from the time of supply), and document any deviation with a customs-broker justification memorandum to prevent fraud characterisation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) – the central bank and monetary authority of Luxembourg; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) – the competent financial sector supervisory authority responsible for the prudential and conduct supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the Economic and Monetary Union and has adopted the euro (EUR) as its sole currency. There are no exchange controls, no restrictions on the convertibility of EUR or other currencies, and no differentiated treatment of current account versus capital account transactions. The EU free movement of capital principle (Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union) applies, meaning that capital contributions, dividends, profit distributions, loan repayments, and trade settlement payments can be freely executed within the EU and between the EU and third jurisdictions subject only to generally applicable anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance, and to EU-level restrictive measures. Profit remittance hurdles are strictly legal/compliance-based rather than FX-control-based; no central bank approval or general permit is required for profit repatriation by an SCSp, provided the entity is in good standing, the beneficial ownership is transparent, and the underlying funds have been sourced and moved in accordance with AML/KYC standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in Luxembourg. Export receipts, including project cargo and heavy haul international transport proceeds, may be retained in their original currency, converted freely, or held in any authorized payment account. There are no mandatory conversion ratios, no forced repatriation timelines, and no requirement to surrender export proceeds to the BCL or any other authority. For statistical balance-of-payments purposes, resident banks may classify cross-border transactions, including the crediting of export proceeds, and report aggregate data to the BCL, but this is an informational statistical obligation and does not create a surrender or repatriation obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational treasury, but Low-Medium for the capital escrow and structural substance layer. Regulated Luxembourg or EEA-passporting electronic money institutions (EMIs) can be utilized for cross-border SWIFT/SEPA payment initiation, FX conversion, and disbursement settlement of project cargo service fees. They are subject to CSSF or home-state financial supervision, the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2), and Anti-Money Laundering Directive (AMLD4/AMLD5) rules. Legal constraints include: EMIs cannot accept deposits or grant credit; safeguarding obligations apply to customer funds; virtual IBAN or sub-account structures may be permitted but require transparent segregation; and certain Luxembourg banks may be unwilling to treat funds held through an EMI as evidence of operational substance. The SCSp's primary commercial banking relationship should remain with a full-license Luxembourg bank to meet preferred banking partner expectations for letter-of-credit operations and large-value project cargo payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: While Luxembourg law and CSSF arrangements allow for certain remote and video-based client onboarding under a risk-based approach, most established Luxembourg commercial banks require at least one physical appearance for each relevant customer-facing principal, particularly for partnerships where a delegated general partner acts with authority. Natural persons performing the role of general partner or senior manager will normally be expected to appear in person before a relationship manager or a Luxembourg-based notary for identity verification. Legal persons need to provide apostilled and notarized corporate documents, board resolutions, and valid identity documents of all ultimate beneficial owners. Remote onboarding, including a video interview with certified document verification, is possible but differs among banks and usually does not eliminate the need for independent verification of the beneficial ownership chain and source of funds. Given the SCSp structure, physical presence of the authorized general partner representatives is mandated in practice for full-service corporate banking with investment-grade banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership chain through the SCSp partnership structure, especially with multiple non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-title records from the SCSp to each ultimate natural person; original or formal certified copy of the limited partnership agreement; register of partners; recent excerpt from the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) showing the registered office, general partner, and authorised signatories; beneficial ownership filing certificate from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); passport copies and proof of residential address of all natural persons in the ownership chain; tax and corporate status certificates for all intermediary entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth insufficiently documented for the capital escrow account receiving inbound project funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or certified financial statements of the contributing partners for the latest two years; bank reference letters and balance statements from the remitting institution; written source-of-wealth statement; supporting contracts, sale agreements, inheritance instruments, or liquidity-producing evidence; notarized declarations confirming the absence of criminal origin of funds; prompt disclosure of any outstanding tax or regulatory dispute in the contributor's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP (politically exposed person) or sanctions-related exposure arising from non-resident limited partners or project counterparties in third-country cargo corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal PEP screening results from a reputable sanctions-compliance data provider; negative media and sanctions list reports for each relevant entity and individual; legal opinion from qualified Luxembourg counsel on the applicability of Luxembourg and EU restrictive measures; contractual indemnities and anti-sanctions certifications from all parties; independent third-party enhanced due diligence report from a licensed corporate agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag associated with out-of-gauge / heavy-haul project cargo logistics due to possible invoice manipulation or over/under-invoicing of transport assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts and order confirmations; itemized project logistics invoices aligned with commercial agreement milestones; relevant bills of lading, cargo manifests, waybills, and customs declarations; independent surveyor or weight/volume verification certificates acceptable to the bank; transit insurance policies and premium payment evidence; project master schedule demonstrating the commercial reality of each milestone payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax opacity due to the SCSp's pass-through tax classification and absence of statutory minimum capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax opinion confirming the SCSp will not be subject to net wealth or corporate income tax in Luxembourg because it is fiscally transparent, with identification of Luxembourg and counterparty tax treatment; the signed partnership agreement and capital account schedule; tax residence certificates of all partners; any issued fiscality request or advance tax decision from the Luxembourg tax authorities if available; certificate of non-existence of any tax registration requirement for the SCSp if relevant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Luxembourg SCSp are executed by international SWIFT MT103 or MT202-compliant wire transfers from the limited partners or their custodians to the SCSp's designated EUR or USD bank account held with a Luxembourg commercial bank. The transfer must clearly reference the currency purpose code and narrative corresponding to a capital contribution, for example 'SCSP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'LIMITED PARTNER SUBSCRIPTION PAYMENT', and the remitting institution must undertake standard KYC/AML verification. Luxembourg banks record cross-border payments for BCL statistics and may request a copy of the call notice, the limited partnership agreement, and a capital contribution schedule. Because Luxembourg applies no exchange controls, no prior central bank approval is required; however, the ultimate beneficial owners and the source of funds must satisfy the bank's amplified EDD requirements for any capital escrow above the bank's internal threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for project cargo and heavy-haul logistics are settled via SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier and subcontractor payments, MT202 for nostro/mirror-account movements, and MT700/MT760 series for documentary letters of credit and standby LC backstops where required by contract. Commercial documentary letters of credit are the preferred rail for high-value outbound disbursements, especially for cross-border freight, port handling, haulage, and oversized cargo equipment purchases. For EUR-denominated payments within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), TARGET2-guaranteed SEPA Credit Transfers provide near-real-time settlement; for USD-denominated or third-currency obligations, the Luxembourg bank will clear through its correspondent banking network, typically via New York or Frankfurt correspondents. SWIFT gpi tracking should be requested to provide transparency and proof of execution for audit and milestone compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright foreign exchange forward contracts
EUR/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) when the project currency is non-convertible or the local deliverable market is inaccessible
EUR/CNY deliverable forwards and CNY NDFs for China-origin heavy-lift equipment and freight payments
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedging dual-currency project financing cash flows
Vanilla EUR currency options and EUR dollar options for premia-protected cash-flow hedging
Range forward contracts and participating forwards to lock in exchange-rate corridors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE), operated via the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 15 March; absolute calendar cut-off, not extendable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to certify RBE data by 15 March triggers administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000; knowingly false or incomplete UBO declarations attract criminal fines from EUR 500 to EUR 12,500. Persistent non-compliance may result in judicial summons and subsequent administrative deregistration of the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing with the Trade and Companies Register (if the SCSp exceeds applicable size thresholds or is a regulated fund vehicle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de commerce et des sociétés – RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory filing deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines range from EUR 50 to EUR 2,000 per initial warning; after two unheeded reminders, the RCS may issue judicial injunction, publish the default in the official journal, and commence administrative strike-off proceedings leading to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Internal Audit of Statutory Registers and Re-affirmation of Registered Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed externally; must be available for immediate RCS and notarial inspection at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous mandatory duty; formal internal verification recommended by 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inaccurate statutory registers constitute a criminal offense under Luxembourg company law, expose partners to unlimited liability in certain cases, and may render partnership-interest transfers unenforceable; inspection failures entail administrative fines and loss of liability protection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds at least two of the following three Luxembourg size criteria during two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 6.2 million; net turnover above EUR 12.4 million; average headcount above 25. A transparent SCSp below these thresholds is generally exempt; however, licensed investment funds (SIF, RAIF/SIF-style SCSp) and SCSp's whose general partner is a limited company may be subject to mandatory audit as a matter of RCS or CSSF prudential requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the law of 19 December 2002 on company account filings, reinforced by Directive 2013/34/EU transposed by the law of 13 July 2016; IFRS applies to consolidated accounts of public-interest entities and may be voluntarily adopted in certain circumscribed cases for SCSp accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually certify, through the RBE web portal, the complete and accurate list of its beneficial owners — natural persons owning or controlling 25% or more of partnership interests, or otherwise exercising ultimate control. The certification must be performed during the fixed 1 January to 15 March window. In the same window, all year-end transfers of partnership units are recorded for RBE re-certification purposes; any in-year change of beneficial ownership requires a separate RBE update within one calendar month from the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited and General Partners (Registre des associés commandités et commanditaires)
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests
Minute Book of Partners' and Management Meetings
Register of Beneficial Ownership Data used for annual RBE cross-check

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level because the SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership; a Luxembourg-resident corporate partner is taxable at a top combined Luxembourg City rate of 24.94% (17% CIT + 7% unemployment-fund surcharge = 18.19%, plus 6.75% municipal business tax) for taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 5229 project cargo operations. Relevant reliefs for corporate partners: 80% IP income box exemption (effective 4.63% corporate tax rate on qualifying IP), 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction on new equity, and loss carry-forward utilising EUR 1,000,000 plus 75% of the excess taxable base. Because the SCSp is transparent, these reliefs are computed at the partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no expiry under LIR Article 110); annual utilisation capped at EUR 1,000,000 + 75% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp Annual Information Filing ('Renseignements annuels') submitted by the general partner via MyGuichet.lu using a LuxTrust e-ID; no CIT form is required for the transparent vehicle itself.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) usually issues a return or request in spring and requires the completed declaration to be returned within three months of service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS filing number (B number), registered office, general partner's details, each limited partner's identity and profit/loss sharing ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign limited partners must state jurisdiction of tax residence, address, Luxembourg PE relevance and the applicable double tax treaty; no Luxembourg WHT is levied on allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable commercial result of the SCSp before allocation; per-partner allocation of profit/loss and capital account movements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Luxembourg-source items (Luxembourg PE income, Luxembourg real estate) to non-resident partners; other income is reportable in the partner's residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forwards, IP box, participation exemption, notional interest deduction and foreign tax credit computations triggered by the SCSp allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) and treaty claim where relief is conditioned on residence or beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Ex officio assessment on failure to file, default interest of 0.6% per commenced month (7.2% per annum), late-filing surcharge up to 10% of the tax assessed, and criminal liability for intentional non-filing (fine and imprisonment).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 160 (corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax declaration) of a Luxembourg-resident corporate partner or general partner, filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / ACDeService.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline of 31 December following the fiscal year-end; the ACD's e-filing practice imposes a shorter deadline of 30 September for 31 December year-ends, with extension to 31 December for electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate partner's name, RCS number, registered office, ISIC 5229 activity code, and percentage share in the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not used by non-resident partners; non-residents file Form 160-T for Luxembourg PE profits only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share of SCSp taxable income, interest and capital gains before loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners are assessed by direct notice on the Luxembourg-source share attributable to a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carried-forward losses offset (EUR 1,000,000 + 75% of excess taxable base).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses attributable to a Luxembourg PE are usable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends or capital gains from an SCSp subsidiary held directly for 12 months with at least 10% participation or an acquisition price of EUR 1,200,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty residence and subject-to-tax conditions must be proven by the partner's home state.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same late-filing default assessment regime; interest at 0.6% per month; penalty up to 10%; criminal sanctions for false declarations; loss of loss-carryforward for the non-filed year.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for SCSp profit allocations — the SCSp has no legal personality and is tax transparent, so distributions are not dividends subject to the Luxembourg 15% statutory dividend WHT. The 15% rate applies only to distributions by resident companies (S.à r.l., SA, SCA, etc.).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is largely irrelevant to SCSp distributions. Where the SCSp receives Luxembourg-source dividends from a portfolio company, the paying company withholds 15%; the foreign partner may recover the excess by (i) submitting Form 166DT / fiscal certificate of beneficial ownership, (ii) presenting a valid TRC from its residence jurisdiction, and (iii) for EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, evidencing the 10% holding (or EUR 1,200,000) and 12-month holding period; the ACD also issues refund vouchers in cases of over-withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 0% WHT on outbound interest and royalties paid by Luxembourg payers, including payments made through an SCSp; treaty rates for dividends are typically 0% (EU PSD), 5% or 10% depending on the DTA, while interest and royalty treaty rates are moot due to the domestic nil rate; ATAD interest limitation rules still apply to corporate partners.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory local currency threshold; the ACD may require Local File/Master File documentation on request (within 30 days). Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to Luxembourg-headquartered or constituent groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000. For the SCSp, contemporaneous documentation should still be prepared whenever related-party transactions exist (e.g., OOG freight, charter, stevedoring and handling services to affiliated shippers).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. Substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (LIR Article 6, ATAD GAAR), the OECD principal-purpose test in DTAs, and ACD audit practice: the SCSp must demonstrate actual local management, physical office and logistics operations, local bank accounts, payroll, and genuine transactions in the OOG heavy-haul business; otherwise profits may be recharacterised and treaty or EU directive benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of SCSp profits, creation of fictitious logistics invoices, misallocation of income to foreign limited partners, or false declarations in the annual filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under the Luxembourg General Tax Act: imprisonment of up to 5 years and/or fine up to EUR 50,000; restitution of evaded tax; default interest of 0.6% per month; late-filing surcharge up to 10% of the assessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (commandité) is jointly and severally liable without limitation; participating directors face personal civil restitution, seizure of assets, travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of contemporaneous TP documentation for related-party OOG cargo, charter and haulage services; unreasonable gross margins; failure to file Country-by-Country Report when group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD upward adjustment of taxable income, recomputed CIT/municipal tax, default interest of 0.6% per month, penalty up to 10% of the deficiency, and separate daily fines for failure to produce requested TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false TP data or direct the SCSp without arm's length controls are personally liable for the assessed shortfall and are exposed to criminal sanctions for false certification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp maintaining only a letterbox presence, decisions taken abroad, no real OOG logistics activity, no personnel or premises, or hybrid mismatch structures creating double non-taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under LIR Article 6 and ATAD GAAR; denial of DTA and EU Directive benefits; reclassification of the SCSp as taxable corporation at 24.94% plus net wealth tax; reassessment for up to 10 years; fines for failure to declare substance changes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner and managing directors are jointly liable for the re-characterised tax, with civil penalties, asset attachment and imprisonment for fraudulent concealment of the arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register/update SCSp beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) or executing milestone wire payments and letter-of-credit operations without basic KYC/AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines between EUR 250 and EUR 125,000 for RBE filing failures; criminal fines for deliberate concealment of beneficial ownership; transaction freezing and adverse regulatory reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner and directors face personal fines, debarment, and imprisonment of up to 5 years where deliberate ML/TF predicate conduct is proven; travel bans may be imposed pending criminal proceedings.
